div.div:
1 قَرَسَ , aor.
قَرِسَ , (S, A, K,) inf, n. قَرْسٌ, (S,) It (cold) was, or became, intense, or vehement; (S, A, K;) as also قَرِسَ, aor.
قَرَسَ , (S, K,) inf. n. قَرَسٌ. (S.) ―
-b2- It (water) became congealed, or frozen. (S, K.) ―
-b3- قرس, inf. n. قرس, [so in the TA, without any syll. signs,] He (a man) was, or became, cold. (TA.) [The verb and its inf. n. in this sense are probably the same as in the sense here next following.] ―
-b4- قُرِسَ, inf. n. قَرْسٌ; (TA;) or قَرِسَ, [inf. n. قَرَسٌ;] (JK;) He (a man smitten by cold) became unable to work (JK, TA) with his hands, (JK,) or with his hand, by reason of the intenseness of the cold, or, as in the L, by reason of cold in his extremities. (TA.) ＝
-A2- قَرَسَ المَآءَ: see 4. ＝
-A3- قَرَسَ قَرِيسًا, (TA,) or ↓ قرّسهُ , (accord. to a copy of the A,) He made, or prepared, what is termed قريس, (A, * TA,) i. e., broth with flesh-meat. (A.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
